repeatRunResult.operationalConclusion: proposalId, recipeRevision, and the full candidateId set were identical across both runs (logical identity is stable/idempotent as designed). Reviewer A returned byte-identical accepted relationships and output hash in both runs; reviewer B non-deterministically accepted 5 additional relationships in run 2 that it had rejected in run 1. In all 5 cases the routingDecision stayed REVIEW_REQUIRED in both runs (unchanged) because deterministic V1 risk evidence (LIFECYCLE_RISK) was present regardless of reviewer agreement, i.e. the risk-gate correctly prevented the reviewer-agreement flip from silently becoming AUTO_ACCEPT. This is expected, architecturally-accepted reviewer nondeterminism per contract §9/§16, not a defect.

findings.finding: AUTO_ACCEPT correctly captured the sear step (oil/potatoes/garlic/herbs) and the butter+steak step. REVIEW_REQUIRED correctly flagged the divided-butter row (QUANTITY_CONFLICT_RISK, since butter is used twice) and the herb-garnish step (LIFECYCLE_RISK, herbs already used once). No nonsensical relationships observed.

AUTO_ACCEPT correctly captured the full toss step (all 6 non-basil ingredients) and the basil-garnish step. REVIEW_REQUIRED correctly flagged the grill/transfer steps referring back to zucchini/squash rows as LIFECYCLE_RISK (continuation of an already-used row) rather than silently auto-accepting reviewer agreement on a continuation. This matches the recipe's selection rationale (whole-dish continuation).

AUTO_ACCEPT correctly captured the plating, basil-tuck, oil/balsamic-drizzle, and salt/pepper-season steps against the exact rows they name. REVIEW_REQUIRED correctly flagged the final 'season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately' step re-firing against tomato/mozzarella/basil/oil as LIFECYCLE_RISK -- a textbook collective/whole-dish reference the router declines to auto-accept even though both reviewers agreed. Matches the recipe's selection rationale (pronoun/collective reference).

AUTO_ACCEPT correctly captured direct sheet-pan additions (kale, salt/pepper), the egg-crack step, and the kimchi-serving step. REVIEW_REQUIRED correctly flagged the final 'divide the rice... divide the vegetables' assembly step against the individual vegetable rows with COMPONENT_CONTAINMENT_RISK + LIFECYCLE_RISK + COLLECTIVE_REFERENCE_RISK stacked together -- exactly the component-boundary/leakage risk class this recipe was selected to exercise, and the router held it to review despite reviewer agreement.

AUTO_ACCEPT correctly captured the single combine-everything step against all 9 listed rows including salt/pepper/oil. Both live reviewers ACCEPTed re-firing salt, pepper, and olive oil against the second (roasting) step -- the exact CONSUMED_ROW-style generic-seasoning false-positive class flagged in the prior offline v10b audit -- but the router correctly downgraded all three to REVIEW_REQUIRED on COMPONENT_CONTAINMENT_RISK + LIFECYCLE_RISK. This is direct live evidence that the V1 risk gate prevents this historically-difficult class from silently auto-accepting even when both live reviewers agree.

semanticSpotCheck.conclusion: No obviously nonsensical relationships were observed in any AUTO_ACCEPT set across the 5 recipes. The single most notable finding is the chickpea-and-fennel-ratatouille case: both live reviewers agreed to accept a generic-seasoning re-trigger (salt/pepper/oil re-fired against a later roasting step) that a prior offline audit had flagged as a false-positive class, and the deterministic V1 risk gate correctly forced that agreement to REVIEW_REQUIRED instead of AUTO_ACCEPT. This is exactly the failure-closed behavior the routing contract is designed to produce and is a positive result, not a concern.
